patch_description: I implemented a hybrid entanglement strategy to improve efficiency and reduce the train-test gap. By replacing fully parameterized CRX ring layers—which often suffer from redundant expressivity or excessive depth when parameters are shared—with a mixture of fixed CZ gates and parameterized CRX gates, the circuit achieves a more robust landscape. Specifically, even-indexed edges (0-1, 2-3, etc.) use fixed CZ gates to provide non-parameterized correlation, while odd-indexed edges (1-2, 3-4, etc.) use CRX gates to inject learnable phase-rotation conditional on control states. This structural variation helps reduce the gate count and depth while maintaining high classification capability.
